title: The Magic Art of the Great Humbug, part 1
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: Next morning the Scarecrow said to his friends:
“Congratulate me. I am going to Oz to get my brains at last. When I return I shall be as other men are.”
“I have always liked you as you were,” said Dorothy simply.

“It is kind of you to like a Scarecrow,” he replied. “But surely you will think more of me when you hear the splendid thoughts my new brain is going to turn out.” Then he said good-bye to them all in a cheerful voice and went to the Throne Room, where he rapped upon the door.
The Scarecrow went in and found the little man sitting down by the window, engaged in deep thought.
“I have come for my brains,” remarked the Scarecrow, a little uneasily.
“Oh, yes; sit down in that chair, please,” replied Oz. “You must excuse me for taking your head off, but I shall have to do it in order to put your brains in their proper place.”
“That’s all right,” said the Scarecrow. “You are quite welcome to take my head off, as long as it will be a better one when you put it on again.”

So the Wizard unfastened his head and emptied out the straw. Then he entered the back room and took up a measure of bran, which he mixed with a great many pins and needles. Having shaken them together thoroughly, he filled the top of the Scarecrow’s head with the mixture and stuffed the rest of the space with straw, to hold it in place.
When he had fastened the Scarecrow’s head on his body again he said to him, “Hereafter you will be a great man, for I have given you a lot of bran-new brains.”
The Scarecrow was both pleased and proud at the fulfillment of his greatest wish, and having thanked Oz warmly he went back to his friends.
Dorothy looked at him curiously. His head was quite bulged out at the top with brains.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Oz say he must do before putting the brains in?
options: Take the Scarecrow's head off
Cut a hole in his breast
Empty the straw from his legs
Repaint his eyes and mouth

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did Oz mix the bran with?
options: A great many pins and needles
A handful of fresh straw
Sawdust and pieces of silk
Oil from the Woodman's can

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what held the mixture in place?
options: Straw stuffed into the rest of the space
A square patch of tin soldered on
A band of green ribbon tied round
Glue painted round the inside of it

questions.prompt: Per the passage, where did the Scarecrow find Oz?
options: Sitting by the window in deep thought
Standing behind the fallen screen
Working in the back room
Asleep upon the green throne

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Dorothy notice about his head?
options: It bulged out at the top
It had shrunk to half its size
It had been painted a new colour
It was covered by a green cap

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did Dorothy say about the old Scarecrow?
options: That she had always liked him as he was
That he had needed brains from the first
That the new head would suit him better
That she hoped he would not change

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the Scarecrow not mind losing his head?
options: He expected a better one to be put back on
He could not feel anything at all
Oz promised to be quick about it
Dorothy had told him to allow it

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did the Scarecrow expect his friends to see him?
options: Thinking more of him once they hear his thoughts
Frightened of how clever he has become
Sorry that he has changed at all from before
Unable to tell any difference in him at all

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what is the joke in bran-new brains?
options: The brains are literally made of bran
The brains are older than they look
Bran is what scarecrows are stuffed with
Bran is a kind of magic powder

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: A wish is granted with bran and pins, and the wisher is delighted
A wizard refuses to give the Scarecrow anything at all
The Scarecrow discovers the Wizard is a humbug
Dorothy persuades the Scarecrow not to change

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Scarecrow say good-bye to his friends?
options: In a cheerful voice
Without a word to anyone
Weeping into his coat sleeve
Only to Dorothy

questions.prompt: Per the passage, how did the Scarecrow speak when he asked for his brains?
options: A little uneasily
Very boldly indeed
In a low whisper
Angrily and loudly

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Oz say the Scarecrow would be hereafter?
options: A great man
A wiser scarecrow
The ruler of the city
A humbug like himself

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did Oz actually do with the old straw?
options: Emptied it out of the head entirely
Mixed it with bran and needles
Left it where it was and added more
Burned it in the back room

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Scarecrow expect the brains to produce?
options: Splendid thoughts
Great strength
A kinder nature
Better eyesight

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does a measure of bran mean?
options: A quantity of it, measured out
A weighing scale for it
A sack it is carried in
A standard of its quality

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: Pins and bran are enough, because the Scarecrow believes in them
The Scarecrow is given real brains by a real wizard
The Scarecrow changes his mind and keeps his straw
Dorothy prevents the Wizard from opening his head
